description: Compute 12-month Net Revenue Retention (NRR) and Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) for June 2025 from monthly MRR snapshots. The base is every customer with mrr > 0 in the snapshot 12 months earlier (June 2024). starting_mrr = their MRR then. For each base customer compare with their MRR now (0 if they have no row or mrr = 0): expansion = sum of increases; contraction = sum of decreases for customers still paying; churned_mrr = starting MRR of customers now at 0. ending_mrr = starting_mrr + expansion - contraction - churned_mrr. nrr = ending_mrr / starting_mrr. grr = (starting_mrr - contraction - churned_mrr) / starting_mrr. Customers who were not in the base (new since) are excluded everywhere. Output columns: month (DATE), starting_mrr, expansion, contraction, churned_mrr, ending_mrr (all FLOAT64), nrr (FLOAT64, 4 decimals), grr (FLOAT64, 4 decimals).

mrr.description: Customer MRR at month end; churned customers have no row or mrr = 0

edge_cases: Customer 2 has no row in June 2025 (churned): contributes 100 to churned_mrr and 0 to ending_mrr
Customer 4 is new since the base month and must be excluded from ending_mrr
GRR ignores expansion and can never exceed 1.0
A customer that churned and came back within the 12 months is judged only by the two endpoint snapshots
common_failure_modes: FM1: INNER JOIN between the two snapshots drops churned customers, inflating NRR (190/150 = 1.27)
FM3: Using total current MRR (390) as ending_mrr includes new customers and yields NRR 1.56
FM2: Comparing with the previous available snapshot instead of exactly 12 calendar months earlier
